clue.text: Compulsory grounding for an aviator

parts.note: grounding sounds like a punishment, but here it is a pilot being obliged to bring the aircraft down early

explanation.surface: A pilot is banned from flying as a penalty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grounding' suggests a teenager or pilot being punished; read literally, it is an aircraft obliged to touch down unplanned.
explanation.definitionFit: An emergency touchdown made because the pilot has no choice is exactly a compelled arrival on the ground.

clue.text: He pours out music from his lyre in Greek mythology

definitions.text: He pours out music from his lyre in Greek mythology

indicators.note: out signals that the letters of he pours are spilled and rearranged

explanation.surface: A legendary Greek figure plays music on his lyre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges HE POURS; the whole clue also describes the mythical musician.
explanation.definitionFit: The legendary Thracian bard of Greek myth charmed beasts and the underworld with the music of his lyre.

clue.text: Student caught with a dictionary

parts.note: C is the cricket scoring abbreviation for caught
the OED is the Oxford English Dictionary

explanation.surface: A student is found holding a dictionary.
explanation.definitionFit: A coeducational student, especially a female one at an American college, is called by this short term.

clue.text: Rubbish collector

parts.note: suggests a refuse worker, but read as the thing in which waste is gathered it is a household container

explanation.definitionFit: A bin for household waste is where refuse gathers before the binmen take it away.

clue.text: Porter is about to dispatch messenger

indicators.note: is about means the beer word goes around the sending word

parts.note: porter is a dark beer, so a kind of ale
to post a letter is to dispatch it

explanation.surface: A railway porter is about to send someone off with a message.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Porter' reads as a railway station worker, but here it is the dark beer; 'is about' means that beer word wraps around the sending word.
explanation.definitionFit: Each of Christ's twelve disciples was sent out to spread the gospel; the Greek root means one sent forth.

clue.text: Expected to end in mortal combat

parts.note: something expected is due

indicators.note: end in picks the final letter of the word mortal

explanation.surface: A fight to the death is anticipated.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal fight between two people, traditionally with pistols or swords, is a single combat.

clue.text: A river once more rises and falls

indicators.note: in a down clue rises means the pieces are read upwards, back to front

parts.note: once more means again

explanation.surface: A river repeatedly swells and subsides.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rises' turns A R AGAIN upward; 'falls' looks like the water level dropping but is the famous waterfall.
explanation.definitionFit: The great waterfalls on the US-Canada border are the best-known cataract in North America.

clue.text: A blow in the back

parts.note: reads like a punch between the shoulders, but blow means a gust of air coming from behind a ship

explanation.definitionFit: A breeze pushing from astern helps a sailing vessel along; sailors prize such a tailwind.

clue.text: Device should catch on, if handled properly

definitions.text: Device should catch on, if handled properly

parts.words: Device should catch on, if handled properly
parts.note: sounds like an invention that should become popular, but catch on is meant literally: a hooked tool that snags a target when thrown well

explanation.definitionFit: A hooked iron tool thrown to seize and hold an enemy ship or a wall is designed to snag and grip.

clue.text: Clamp down on work force

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a work
to press is to force

explanation.surface: Authorities crack down on the labour force.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep people under harsh authority is to crush or subjugate them, as a tyrant does.

clue.text: Available to discuss outside

parts.note: open means available, as an open position
to air a matter is to discuss it publicly

explanation.surface: Someone is free to talk things over outdoors.
explanation.definitionFit: Something held outdoors rather than under a roof takes place in the fresh air.

clue.text: Place where economy of truth is fashionable

parts.note: a whimsical phrase for a falsehood
U means upper-class, hence fashionable

explanation.surface: Somewhere being economical with the truth is in vogue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Being economical with the truth' is a famous British euphemism for lying.
explanation.definitionFit: The word survives in the phrase meaning instead of, where it denotes stead or position.

clue.text: Skip a beat and reduce

indicators.note: skip suggests the letters of a beat jump about into a new order

explanation.surface: A heart misses a beat and slows down.
explanation.definitionFit: To lessen or diminish, as a storm or fever dies down.

clue.text: Jar for a kind of berry

definitions.meaning: to jar is to grate harshly on the ear or nerves
a shortening of the red soft fruit's name

explanation.surface: A jar is used for storing berries.
explanation.definitionFit: A grating sound jars on the ear, and the word is also an informal clipping of a red cane-fruit's name.

clue.text: Commonest name for a forger

definitions.meaning: the most frequent surname in the English-speaking world
one who forges metal, not a counterfeiter

explanation.surface: A forger usually signs with the most common surname.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forger' suggests a counterfeiter but means a metalworker at a forge.
explanation.definitionFit: A blacksmith works iron at a forge, and the occupational surname is the most frequent in Britain.

clue.text: A mouthful of water!

parts.note: sounds like a gulp drunk, but it is the triangular area where a river meets the sea at its mouth

explanation.definitionFit: A river's mouth often spreads into a fan of silt and channels, as at the Nile.

clue.text: The Magi seem upset in victory

indicators.note: in places the rearranged letters inside the victory word

parts.note: a victory is a win

indicators.note: upset means the letters of seem are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: The three kings look troubled despite winning.
explanation.definitionFit: The Magi were the learned visitors from the East who brought gifts to the infant Jesus.

clue.text: Sphere of vision

parts.note: sounds like a field of view, but sphere is literal: the round organ that sees

explanation.definitionFit: The globe of the human organ of sight is a literal ball.

clue.text: Journey on such a train can only have one end

definitions.text: Journey on such a train can only have one end

parts.words: Journey on such a train can only have one end
parts.note: a service that never halts on the way cannot stop at any intermediate station, only its terminus

explanation.definitionFit: An express that makes no intermediate halts runs without a break from origin to destination.

clue.text: Ancient city in part of South Africa is unaffected

indicators.note: in places the city inside the province

parts.note: Natal is a South African province
Ur was an ancient Sumerian city

explanation.surface: An old city in a South African region was spared harm.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone without airs or pretence behaves in a genuine, spontaneous way.

clue.text: US sportsman in jug

definitions.meaning: the baseball player who throws to the batter
a large jug with a lip for pouring

explanation.surface: An American athlete is in prison.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jug' suggests jail (British slang), but it is a pouring vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: In baseball the player who throws to the batter shares a name with a large pouring vessel.

clue.text: Comfortable seat for a Turk

definitions.meaning: a low padded footstool or couch without a back
a member of the former Turkish empire

explanation.surface: A Turkish man gets a cosy chair.
explanation.definitionFit: A padded backless couch takes its name from the Turkish empire, whose subjects bore the same name.

clue.text: Imply small company is involved in games, perhaps

indicators.note: is involved means the letters are tangled together and rearranged

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company

explanation.surface: A small firm hints it is taking part in some games.
explanation.definitionFit: The world's great multi-sport contest is the most famous example of international games.

clue.text: Oratorio is a new production in the network

indicators.note: in places them inside the network word

parts.note: a mesh is a network

indicators.note: new production means the letters of is a are staged in a fresh order

explanation.surface: A new staging of a choral work is going out on the broadcasting network.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new production' turns IS A into SIA; the surface suggests a broadcast on a TV network, but the network is a net.
explanation.definitionFit: Handel's best-known sacred choral work, first performed in Dublin in 1742, tells the story of Christ.

clue.text: Put point to a teetotal engineer

parts.note: W, west, is a compass point

explanation.surface: Someone directs a sober engineer.
explanation.definitionFit: James Watt was the Scottish engineer who improved the steam engine; the unit of power is named after him.

clue.text: Checks part of the rigging

definitions.meaning: ... as a verb means halts or restrains
ropes that brace a ship's mast

explanation.surface: Someone inspects a section of a ship's ropes.
explanation.definitionFit: To halt something is to restrain it, and the ropes bracing a mast fore and aft share the name.

clue.text: It's drunk in the East Indies

indicators.note: in signals that the answer sits within the words East Indies

explanation.surface: Something is consumed in the East Indies.
explanation.definitionFit: A sparkling white wine from Piedmont in Italy is drunk the world over.

clue.text: Revolutionary entertainment

parts.note: sounds political, but revolutionary means spinning, as a record does on a turntable

explanation.definitionFit: A gramophone record or CD spins on its player, providing music as it turns.

clue.text: Baked beans need this lid for protection

definitions.text: Baked beans need this lid for protection

parts.words: Baked beans need this lid for protection
parts.note: beans is slang for heads, baked means scorched by the sun, and lid is slang for a hat

explanation.walkthrough: 'beans' is old slang for heads and 'lid' for a hat, so the clue is about shading sunburnt heads, not a tin.
explanation.definitionFit: A pith helmet worn in hot countries protects the head from the sun.

clue.text: Eastern city doctor, now rich

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so the letters of now rich are altered

explanation.surface: A doctor in an East Anglian city has become wealthy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doctor' looks like a person but is the anagram verb; Norwich is the county city of Norfolk, in eastern England.
explanation.definitionFit: The cathedral city of Norfolk lies in East Anglia, the eastern bulge of England.

clue.text: Violet's in unusually poor condition

indicators.note: in places Violet's letters inside the rearranged word
unusually means the letters of poor are arranged in an unexpected way

parts.note: VI is short for the name Violet, plus the S of the possessive

explanation.surface: Violet is in unusually bad shape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusually' turns the letters of the word poor into PROO; Violet looks like a flower but is the girl's name, shortened.
explanation.definitionFit: A clause in an agreement that sets a requirement is a stipulation attached to it.

clue.text: The Celtic girl out to provide illumination

indicators.note: out suggests the letters of the Celtic girl are thrown out of order

explanation.surface: A Celtic girl goes out to fetch a lamp.
explanation.definitionFit: Lamps powered by the mains are the commonest modern source of illumination.
